front_prompt: 5. Describe the historical significance of the Madhya Rekhā in ancient Indian astronomy.
back_answer: Over 1,500 years ago, ancient Indian astronomers like Varāhamihira established a prime meridian called the Madhya Rekhā ('middle line') passing through Ujjain (75.8° E). Ujjain served as a major astronomical research center, and this meridian served as the zero reference line for timekeeping and planetary calculations in classical Indian texts long before the Greenwich meridian was internationally adopted.
